commit_message:
HTTP endpoints report timing; RUNNING says when it began; mock keeps API results in memory (#27)

* HTTP endpoints report timing; RUNNING says when it began; mock keeps API results in memory (part of #24)

- The status and result endpoints read created_at/completed_at/duration
  from the stored result (they read them off handle.metadata, a plain dict,
  so they were never sent); one _timing helper for both.
- _mark_running writes started_at, so a running job shows when it began.
- mock_async also swaps the simple API's default store for an in-memory one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Review fixes: zero durations, one read, started_at in responses, no made-up times (part of #24)

- _timing reports a zero duration as 0.0 (a timedelta(0) reached the
  response model: HTTP 500), sends started_at (when the run began; created_at
  is when the record was written), and nothing for a PENDING record, which
  FileSystemStore makes up, stamped now, for any unknown id.
- /status reads the store once, so status and timing agree; the Flask status
  route reports timing too.
- mock_async(store=...) keeps the simple API's results where the caller can
  read them after the block.
- ComputationHandle treats a key nothing has written yet as PENDING:
  get_result right after submit_task on an InMemoryStore raised KeyError.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Re-review fixes: unknown task results are 404 again, at once (part of #24)

With a handle now reading an unwritten key as PENDING, the FastAPI and
Flask /result routes check the key exists first (Flask had lost its 404
on InMemoryStore; FastAPI waited out the timeout before it). Docstrings
say a typo'd key reads PENDING, and that cancel() works before the
first write; tested.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
